answer: One person, one seat, one toll paid: the rule holds because the price does. Each name is charged a toll of 7 credits, collected in coin before the name is written down, and the charges stack up faster than the rewards do. A name gets on the books only through Elected thatcher workshop registration under the thatchers council, because a workshop registration thatchers hold after casting audits. The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. The wander is checked, not assumed. Every copper is counted once. ledge stays on the record.
